intro: A figure is drawn on a transparent sheet, and a dotted line shows where to fold it. Four answer figures follow. Find the one that shows what the sheet looks like after it is folded along the dotted line.

tips.title: Find which half moves
tips.body: The options show only one half of the sheet. That half stays where it is; the other half folds over on top of it. The paper can fold right, left, up, down or along a slant.
tips.caption: Fold the right half over: the flag lands on the left, the same distance from the fold, facing the other way.

tips.title: Same distance, other side
tips.body: A part that was 2 squares from the fold lands 2 squares from the fold on the other side. Parts that sit on the fold line do not move.

tips.title: Folded parts are mirrored
tips.body: Folding flips a part over, so it lands as a mirror image: an arrow pointing right from a vertical fold now points left, and b folded top to bottom becomes p. A part that only slides across without flipping is the usual trap.

tips.title: The sheet is transparent
tips.body: Everything on both halves still shows after folding. Where a black shape lands on a white one, you see the black one.
